headline: Trading volumes and higher rates lift profit broadly
summary_short: Interactive Brokers grew Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS 35% y/y to $0.69 and net income 39% y/y to $312M, as net interest income rose to $1.06 billion and commission revenue grew to $673 million on higher trading volumes.
summary_long: Commission revenue rose 30% y/y to $673M on higher options, stock, and futures volumes, while net interest income rose 23% y/y to $1.06B on larger customer margin loans and credit balances; other fees and services rose 40% to $87M. Diluted EPS of $0.69 was up 35% y/y and 17% q/q; income before taxes rose to $1.46B (+32% y/y), holding pretax margin at 77% versus 75% a year ago. Cash and equivalents jumped to $7.71B from $5.09B q/q as customer margin loans grew to $108.5B and customer credit balances to $182.4B. The board declared a $0.0875/share quarterly dividend; no forward guidance was issued.

Basis note: the shard's revenue_usd_m KPI ($760M, tagged RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) is ASC 606 contract revenue only — commissions ($673M) plus other fees and services ($87M) — and is NOT the release's headline 'net revenues' figure ($1.896B GAAP / $1.883B adjusted), which additionally includes $1.057B of net interest income that falls outside ASC 606 scope for a broker-dealer. Readers comparing our Commission & fee revenue KPI to the press release's own $1.90B headline number should not expect them to match; this is a structural feature of how revenue is defined for financial-services issuers, not a data error. The shard's Yahoo-derived ebitda_usd_m/ebit_usd_m/gross_profit_usd_m/operating_income_usd_m KPIs were excluded from this summary entirely: IBKR's income statement has no natural COGS/opex split (it is a broker-dealer), so those Yahoo template-fit figures don't correspond to any line the company itself discloses and would be misleading if presented as company-reported metrics. GAAP and adjusted diluted EPS were identical this quarter ($0.69 both); GAAP and adjusted net revenues differed slightly ($1.896B vs $1.883B) due to currency-diversification and mark-to-market non-GAAP adjustments — the shard's pretax_income_usd_m ($1.456B) is the GAAP figure, distinct from the release's adjusted pretax income of $1.443B.

drivers.explanation: Commission revenue rose 30% to $673M on higher options, stock, and futures trading volumes (+17%, +14%, +2% respectively); other fees and services rose 40% to $87M, led by higher order-flow payments, risk exposure fees, and market data fees.

Net interest income grew 23% to $1.06B on higher average customer margin loans and credit balances; execution, clearing and distribution fees rose 22% to $142M on higher SEC Section 31 fees, partly offset by greater liquidity-rebate capture.
EPS growth tracked net income growth closely rather than buybacks — diluted share count rose only modestly, to 450.1M from 441.4M a year ago.
Pretax margin held at 77% (reported and adjusted), up from 75% a year ago, as commission and net-interest-income growth outpaced the rise in non-interest expenses.
Not separately explained in the release; the cash build coincided with customer margin loans rising 67% y/y to $108.5B and customer credit balances rising 27% to $182.4B.
Not explained in the release beyond the consolidated $22.3B total-equity figure, which includes noncontrolling interests and is not reconciled separately to IBG, Inc.'s standalone equity share.
Growth was broad-based across commissions, net interest income, and fee income; the board declared an unchanged $0.0875/share quarterly dividend and the release issued no forward guidance.
